nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-01.title: Arithmetic series
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-01.body:
With $n$ piles of $3,4,\dots,n+2$ coins, the total is $\frac n2(3+(n+2))=\frac{n(n+5)}{2}=150$. So $n^2+5n-300=0$, $(n+20)(n-15)=0$, and $n=15$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-01.title: Subtract a triangular number
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-01.body:
$3+4+\dots+m=\frac{m(m+1)}2-3=150$ gives $m(m+1)=306=17\cdot18$, so the largest pile is $17$ and the piles are $3,\dots,17$: $15$ piles.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-03.title: Count pairs
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-03.body:
With $n$ people there are $\binom n2=\frac{n(n-1)}2$ handshakes. $n(n-1)=306=18\cdot17$, so $n=18$.

**Answer: 18**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-03.title: Add up
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-03.body:
The $k$-th person to arrive shakes hands with the $k-1$ already present, so the total is $1+2+\dots+(n-1)$. $1+2+\dots+17=153$, so $n-1=17$ and $n=18$.

**Answer: 18**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-04.title: Parity of $y$
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-04.body:
$x=\frac{1009-3y}{2}$ is a positive integer exactly when $y$ is odd and $3y<1009$, i.e. $y\le335$. The odd numbers $1,3,\dots,335$ number $168$.

**Answer: 168**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-04.title: Parametrise
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-04.body:
One solution is $(x,y)=(503,1)$; all integer solutions are $x=503-3t$, $y=1+2t$. Positivity needs $t\ge0$ and $503-3t\ge1$, i.e. $t\le167$. So $t=0,\dots,167$: $168$ solutions.

**Answer: 168**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-05.title: Twelve triangles
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-05.body:
Radii to the vertices cut the dodecagon into $12$ triangles with two sides $5$ and included angle $30^\circ$, each of area $\frac12\cdot5\cdot5\sin30^\circ=\frac{25}4$. Total $12\cdot\frac{25}4=75$.

**Answer: 75**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-05.title: General formula
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-05.body:
A regular $n$-gon inscribed in a circle of radius $r$ has area $\frac n2r^2\sin\frac{360^\circ}{n}$. For $n=12$: $6r^2\sin30^\circ=3r^2=75$.

**Answer: 75**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-06.title: Complete the cube
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-06.body:
$3150=2\cdot3^2\cdot5^2\cdot7$. To make every exponent a multiple of $3$, multiply by $2^2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7^2=2940$. Then $3150\cdot2940=2^3 3^3 5^3 7^3=210^3$.

**Answer: 2940**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-06.title: Check minimality
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-06.body:
Any $x$ that works must supply at least two more $2$'s, one more $3$, one more $5$ and two more $7$'s, so $x$ is a multiple of $2940$. The smallest is $2940$, with $N=210$.

**Answer: 2940**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-08.title: Seat men, then women
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-08.body:
Seat the men first in alternate seats; up to rotation there are $3!=6$ arrangements. The four seats between them are then distinguishable, and the women fill them in $4!=24$ ways. Total $6\cdot24=144$.

**Answer: 144**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-08.title: Divide by rotations
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-08.body:
Fixing alternating positions, there are $2$ choices of which set of seats the men take, then $4!\cdot4!$ arrangements, giving $2\cdot576=1152$ seatings at a table with labelled seats. Dividing by the $8$ rotations: $\frac{1152}8=144$.

**Answer: 144**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-10.title: Speed ratio
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-10.body:
Half the time for the same distance means the downstream speed is twice the upstream speed: $5+c=2(5-c)$, giving $3c=5$, $c=\frac53$ mph.

**Answer: $\frac53$ mph**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-11.title: Repeated division
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-11.body:
Divide by $3$ repeatedly: $1000=3\cdot333+1$, $333=3\cdot111+0$, $111=3\cdot37+0$, $37=3\cdot12+1$, $12=3\cdot4+0$, $4=3\cdot1+1$, $1=3\cdot0+1$. Reading the remainders upward: $1101001_3$.

**Answer: $1101001$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-12.title: Pythagoras
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-12.body:
Let the base be $2x$ and the legs $y$. Then $2x+2y=20$, so $y=10-x$, and $y^2=x^2+25$. So $(10-x)^2=x^2+25$, $100-20x=25$, $x=3.75$. Area $=\frac12\cdot2x\cdot5=5x=18.75$.

**Answer: 18.75**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-12.title: Difference of squares
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-12.body:
In the half-triangle, $y^2-x^2=25$ and $y+x=10$, so $y-x=2.5$, giving $x=3.75$, $y=6.25$. Area $=x\cdot5=18.75$.

**Answer: 18.75**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-13.title: Solve explicitly
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-13.body:
The numbers are roots of $t^2-20t+30=0$: $10\pm\sqrt{70}$. Then $\frac1{10+\sqrt{70}}+\frac1{10-\sqrt{70}}=\frac{20}{100-70}=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-14.title: Two right triangles
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-14.body:
Let the altitude $h$ split the side $8$ into $x$ (next to side $7$) and $8-x$ (next to side $3$). Then $h^2=49-x^2=9-(8-x)^2$, so $49-x^2=9-64+16x-x^2$, $16x=104$, $x=6\frac12$.

**Answer: $6\frac12$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-14.title: Projection formula
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-14.body:
The segments are the projections of the other two sides onto the side of length $8$. The projection of side $7$ onto side $8$ is $\frac{7^2+8^2-3^2}{2\cdot8}=\frac{104}{16}=6.5$, and the other is $8-6.5=1.5$. The longer is $6.5$.

**Answer: $6\frac12$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-15.title: Equation
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-15.body:
With $d$ dogs and $w$ women: $4d+2w=22+2(d+w)$, so $2d=22$ and $d=11$.

**Answer: 11**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-15.title: Extra legs
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-15.body:
Every head comes with at least $2$ legs; each dog has $2$ legs beyond that and each woman none. So the $22$ extra legs come from $\frac{22}2=11$ dogs.

**Answer: 11**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-18.title: Two conjugates
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-18.body:
Multiply by $\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$: the denominator becomes $(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^2-5=2\sqrt6$ and the numerator $2+\sqrt6+\sqrt{10}$. Multiply top and bottom by $\sqrt6$: $\frac{2\sqrt6+6+2\sqrt{15}}{12}=\frac{3+\sqrt6+\sqrt{15}}{6}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3+\sqrt6+\sqrt{15}}{6}$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-20.title: Add rates
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-20.body:
Per hour: four old printers do $\frac4{10}$ and three new ones $\frac36$, together $\frac25+\frac12=\frac9{10}$ of a newspaper. Time $=\frac{10}{9}=1\frac19$ hours.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{9}$ hours**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-21.title: Exponential form
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-21.body:
$x=\log_{3x}36$ means $(3x)^x=36$. Trying $x=2$: $6^2=36$ ✓. For $x>\frac13$ the function $(3x)^x$ is increasing (both base and exponent grow) and for $0<x\le\frac13$ it is at most $1$, so $x=2$ is the only solution.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-21.title: Take logs
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-21.body:
$x\ln(3x)=\ln36=2\ln6$. The left side is increasing for $x\ge\frac13$, and $x=2$ gives $2\ln6$. So $x=2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-23.title: Treat as a quadratic in $x$
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-23.body:
For real $x$ the discriminant $100-4(y^2-12y+61)=-4(y-6)^2$ must be $\ge0$, forcing $y=6$; then $x^2+10x+25=0$ gives $x=-5$.

**Answer: $(-5,6)$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-24.title: British flag theorem
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-24.body:
Draw lines through $P$ parallel to the sides; each squared distance to a corner splits into two squared pieces. This gives $PA^2+PC^2=PB^2+PD^2$, so $9+25=16+PD^2$, $PD^2=18$ and $PD=3\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-25.title: Totals
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-25.body:
Total $=30\cdot80=2400$. Removing $97+75+95=267$ leaves $2133$ for $27$ students: average $\frac{2133}{27}=79$.

**Answer: 79**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-25.title: Deviations
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-25.body:
Relative to $80$, the three removed marks deviate by $+17,-5,+15$, total $+27$. The remaining $27$ marks must deviate by $-27$ in total, i.e. $-1$ each on average: $79$.

**Answer: 79**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-27.title: Remove the logarithm
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-27.body:
$x^2+5x-50=100$, so $x^2+5x-150=0$, $(x+15)(x-10)=0$: $x=10$ or $x=-15$. Both make the argument $100>0$, so both are valid.

**Answer: $10$ and $-15$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-29.title: Right trapezoid
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-29.body:
The centres are $4+6=10$ apart. The radii to the tangent points are parallel (both perpendicular to the tangent), so dropping a perpendicular from the small centre to the large radius gives a right triangle with hypotenuse $10$ and leg $6-4=2$. The tangent segment equals the other leg: $\sqrt{100-4}=\sqrt{96}=4\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt6$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-29.title: Formula
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-29.body:
For externally tangent circles the common external tangent has length $\sqrt{(r_1+r_2)^2-(r_1-r_2)^2}=2\sqrt{r_1r_2}=2\sqrt{24}=4\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt6$**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-30.title: Factor pairs
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-30.body:
$(a+b)(a-b)=105$ with $a+b>a-b\ge1$, both odd. The factor pairs are $105\cdot1$, $35\cdot3$, $21\cdot5$, $15\cdot7$, giving $(a,b)=(53,52),(19,16),(13,8),(11,4)$. So $4$ solutions.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-30.title: Count divisors
nyciml-1991-92-spring-seniorb-30.body:
$105=3\cdot5\cdot7$ has $8$ divisors, forming $4$ pairs $(d,\frac{105}d)$ with $d<\frac{105}{d}$. All divisors are odd, so each pair gives integer $a=\frac{d+105/d}2$, $b=\frac{105/d-d}2>0$. Hence $4$ solutions.

**Answer: 4**
